decls.name: TauCeti.Nat.Partition.equivSortedParts
decls.doc: A partition is equivalent to its decreasing list of positive parts.

decls.name: TauCeti.Nat.Partition.equivSortedParts_apply_coe
decls.doc: Sorting the parts is the forward map of `equivSortedParts`.
decls.statement:
theorem equivSortedParts_apply_coe (n : ℕ) (p : n.Partition) :
    (equivSortedParts n p).1 = p.parts.sort (· ≥ ·)

decls.name: TauCeti.Nat.Partition.equivSortedParts_symm_apply_parts
decls.doc: The inverse of `equivSortedParts` has the given list as its multiset of parts.
decls.statement:
theorem equivSortedParts_symm_apply_parts (n : ℕ)
    (w : {w : List ℕ // (w.SortedGE ∧ ∀ x ∈ w, 0 < x) ∧ w.sum = n}) :
    ((equivSortedParts n).symm w).parts = w.1

decls.name: TauCeti.sum_take_rowLens_eq_card_filter_fst
decls.statement:
theorem sum_take_rowLens_eq_card_filter_fst (μ : YoungDiagram) (k : ℕ) :
    (μ.rowLens.take k).sum = (μ.cells.filter fun c => c.1 < k).card

decls.name: TauCeti.sum_map_min_rowLens_eq_card_filter_snd
decls.statement:
theorem sum_map_min_rowLens_eq_card_filter_snd (μ : YoungDiagram) (k : ℕ) :
    (μ.rowLens.map (min k)).sum = (μ.cells.filter fun c => c.2 < k).card

decls.name: TauCeti.card_filter_fst_transpose
decls.statement:
theorem card_filter_fst_transpose (μ : YoungDiagram) (k : ℕ) :
    (μ.transpose.cells.filter fun c => c.1 < k).card =
      (μ.cells.filter fun c => c.2 < k).card

decls.name: TauCeti.sum_take_transpose_rowLens
decls.statement:
theorem sum_take_transpose_rowLens (μ : YoungDiagram) (k : ℕ) :
    (μ.transpose.rowLens.take k).sum = (μ.rowLens.map (min k)).sum

decls.name: TauCeti.sum_sub_add_mul_length_takeWhile
decls.statement:
theorem sum_sub_add_mul_length_takeWhile {l : List ℕ} (hl : l.SortedGE) (k : ℕ) :
    (l.map fun x => x - k).sum +
        k * (l.takeWhile fun x => decide (k < x)).length =
      (l.takeWhile fun x => decide (k < x)).sum

decls.name: TauCeti.sum_take_le_mul_add_sum_sub
decls.statement:
theorem sum_take_le_mul_add_sum_sub (l : List ℕ) (k r : ℕ) :
    (l.take r).sum ≤ k * r + (l.map fun x => x - k).sum

decls.name: TauCeti.sum_min_add_sum_sub
decls.statement:
theorem sum_min_add_sum_sub (l : List ℕ) (k : ℕ) :
    (l.map (min k)).sum + (l.map fun x => x - k).sum = l.sum

decls.name: TauCeti.sum_map_min_le_of_prefix_sum_le
decls.statement:
theorem sum_map_min_le_of_prefix_sum_le {l₁ l₂ : List ℕ}
    (hl₂ : l₂.SortedGE) (hsum : l₁.sum = l₂.sum)
    (hle : ∀ r, (l₂.take r).sum ≤ (l₁.take r).sum) (k : ℕ) :
    (l₁.map (min k)).sum ≤ (l₂.map (min k)).sum

decls.name: TauCeti.diagramOf
decls.doc: The Young diagram of a partition.
decls.statement: def diagramOf {n : ℕ} (μ : n.Partition) : YoungDiagram

decls.name: TauCeti.diagramOf_injective
decls.doc: The Young diagram construction is injective on partitions of a fixed size.
decls.statement: theorem diagramOf_injective {n : ℕ} : Function.Injective (diagramOf (n := n))

decls.name: TauCeti.card_diagramOf
decls.doc: The Young diagram of a partition has the size of the partition.
decls.statement: theorem card_diagramOf {n : ℕ} (μ : n.Partition) : (diagramOf μ).card = n

decls.name: TauCeti.rowLens_diagramOf
decls.doc: The row lengths of a partition's Young diagram are its decreasingly sorted parts.
decls.statement:
theorem rowLens_diagramOf {n : ℕ} (μ : n.Partition) :
    (diagramOf μ).rowLens = μ.parts.sort (· ≥ ·)

decls.name: TauCeti.conjugate
decls.doc: The conjugate of a partition is obtained by transposing its Young diagram.
decls.statement: def conjugate {n : ℕ} (μ : n.Partition) : n.Partition

decls.name: TauCeti.diagramOf_conjugate
decls.doc: The Young diagram of the conjugate partition is the transposed Young diagram.
decls.statement:
theorem diagramOf_conjugate {n : ℕ} (μ : n.Partition) :
    diagramOf (conjugate μ) = (diagramOf μ).transpose

decls.name: TauCeti.conjugate_conjugate
decls.doc: Conjugating a partition twice recovers the original partition.
decls.statement:
theorem conjugate_conjugate {n : ℕ} (μ : n.Partition) :
    conjugate (conjugate μ) = μ

decls.name: TauCeti.conjugate_parts_sort
decls.doc:
The decreasing parts of the conjugate partition are the row lengths of the transposed
diagram.
decls.statement:
theorem conjugate_parts_sort {n : ℕ} (μ : n.Partition) :
    (conjugate μ).parts.sort (· ≥ ·) = (diagramOf μ).transpose.rowLens

decls.name: TauCeti.dominates_conjugate
decls.statement:
theorem dominates_conjugate {n : ℕ} {μ ν : n.Partition} (h : Dominates μ ν) :
    Dominates (conjugate ν) (conjugate μ)

decls.name: TauCeti.dominates_conjugate_iff
decls.doc: Conjugation of partitions reverses dominance.
decls.statement:
theorem dominates_conjugate_iff {n : ℕ} (μ ν : n.Partition) :
    Dominates μ ν ↔ Dominates (conjugate ν) (conjugate μ)

decls.name: TauCeti.sortedParts
decls.statement: abbrev sortedParts {n : ℕ} (μ : n.Partition) : List ℕ

decls.name: TauCeti.sortedParts_sum
decls.statement:
theorem sortedParts_sum {n : ℕ} (μ : n.Partition) :
    (sortedParts μ).sum = n

decls.name: TauCeti.sortedParts_length_le
decls.statement:
theorem sortedParts_length_le {n : ℕ} (μ : n.Partition) :
    (sortedParts μ).length ≤ n

decls.name: TauCeti.PartitionLex.partitionLinearOrder
decls.doc:
The lexicographic linear order on partitions, obtained from their decreasingly sorted parts.
Activate it with `open scoped TauCeti.PartitionLex`.
decls.statement: instance partitionLinearOrder {n : ℕ} : LinearOrder n.Partition

decls.name: TauCeti.PartitionLex.partition_lt_iff
decls.doc:
Partition comparison in the lexicographic order is comparison of the decreasingly sorted
parts.

decls.name: TauCeti.PartitionLex.partition_le_iff
decls.doc:
Partition comparison in the non-strict lexicographic order is comparison of the decreasingly
sorted parts.

decls.name: TauCeti.Dominates
decls.doc:
A partition `μ` dominates a partition `ν` when every partial sum of the decreasingly
sorted parts of `μ` is at least the corresponding partial sum of `ν`.
decls.statement: def Dominates {n : ℕ} (μ ν : n.Partition) : Prop

decls.name: TauCeti.dominates_def
decls.doc: By definition, dominance compares the first `n + 1` partial sums.
decls.statement:
theorem dominates_def {n : ℕ} {μ ν : n.Partition} :
    Dominates μ ν ↔
      ∀ k : Fin (n + 1),
        ((ν.parts.sort (· ≥ ·)).take k).sum ≤
          ((μ.parts.sort (· ≥ ·)).take k).sum

decls.name: TauCeti.dominates_iff
decls.doc: The defining partial-sum characterization of dominance.
decls.statement:
theorem dominates_iff {n : ℕ} {μ ν : n.Partition} :
    Dominates μ ν ↔
      ∀ k : ℕ,
        ((ν.parts.sort (· ≥ ·)).take k).sum ≤
          ((μ.parts.sort (· ≥ ·)).take k).sum

decls.name: TauCeti.instDecidableDominates
decls.statement: instance {n : ℕ} (μ ν : n.Partition) : Decidable (Dominates μ ν)

decls.name: TauCeti.dominates_refl
decls.doc: Every partition dominates itself.
decls.statement: theorem dominates_refl {n : ℕ} (μ : n.Partition) : Dominates μ μ

decls.name: TauCeti.Dominates.trans
decls.doc: Dominance is transitive.
decls.statement:
theorem Dominates.trans {n : ℕ} {μ ν ξ : n.Partition}
    (hμν : Dominates μ ν) (hνξ : Dominates ν ξ) : Dominates μ ξ

decls.name: TauCeti.lex_lt_of_prefix_sum_le
decls.statement:
theorem lex_lt_of_prefix_sum_le {l₁ l₂ : List ℕ}
    (hsum : l₁.sum = l₂.sum)
    (hpos₁ : ∀ i ∈ l₁, 0 < i) (hpos₂ : ∀ i ∈ l₂, 0 < i)
    (hle : ∀ k : ℕ, (l₂.take k).sum ≤ (l₁.take k).sum)
    (hne : l₁ ≠ l₂) : l₂ < l₁

decls.name: TauCeti.lex_lt_of_dominates_of_ne
TauCeti.Dominates.antisymm
decls.doc: Dominance is antisymmetric.
decls.statement:
theorem Dominates.antisymm {n : ℕ} {μ ν : n.Partition}
    (hμν : Dominates μ ν) (hνμ : Dominates ν μ) : μ = ν

decls.name: TauCeti.DominanceOrder.partitionPartialOrder
decls.doc:
The dominance partial order on partitions, oriented so that `ν ≤ μ` means that `μ`
dominates `ν`. Activate it with `open scoped TauCeti.DominanceOrder`.
decls.statement: instance partitionPartialOrder {n : ℕ} : PartialOrder n.Partition

decls.name: TauCeti.DominanceOrder.partition_le_iff
decls.doc: Partition comparison in the dominance order is dominance in the reverse direction.
decls.statement:
theorem partition_le_iff {n : ℕ} {μ ν : n.Partition} :
    @LE.le n.Partition partitionPartialOrder.toLE μ ν ↔ Dominates ν μ

decls.name: TauCeti.DominanceOrder.partition_lt_iff
decls.doc:
Strict partition comparison in the dominance order is strict dominance in the reverse
direction.
decls.statement:
theorem partition_lt_iff {n : ℕ} {μ ν : n.Partition} :
    @LT.lt n.Partition partitionPartialOrder.toLT μ ν ↔ Dominates ν μ ∧ μ ≠ ν

decls.name: TauCeti.StrictlyDominates
decls.doc: Strict dominance is the strict relation of the dominance partial order.
decls.statement: def StrictlyDominates {n : ℕ} (μ ν : n.Partition) : Prop

decls.name: TauCeti.strictlyDominates_iff
decls.doc: Strict dominance is dominance between unequal partitions.
decls.statement:
theorem strictlyDominates_iff {n : ℕ} {μ ν : n.Partition} :
    StrictlyDominates μ ν ↔ Dominates μ ν ∧ μ ≠ ν

decls.name: TauCeti.instIsStrictOrderPartitionStrictlyDominates
decls.doc:
Strict dominance is a strict order on partitions, inherited from the dominance partial
order.
decls.statement: instance {n : ℕ} : IsStrictOrder n.Partition StrictlyDominates

decls.name: TauCeti.instDecidableStrictlyDominates
decls.statement: instance {n : ℕ} (μ ν : n.Partition) : Decidable (StrictlyDominates μ ν)

decls.name: TauCeti.lex_lt_of_strictlyDominates
decls.doc: Strict dominance refines the lexicographic linear order on partitions.
decls.statement:
theorem lex_lt_of_strictlyDominates {n : ℕ} {μ ν : n.Partition}
    (h : StrictlyDominates μ ν) : ν < μ

decls.name: TauCeti.lex_le_of_dominates
decls.doc: Dominance refines the lexicographic linear order on partitions.
decls.statement: theorem lex_le_of_dominates {n : ℕ} {μ ν : n.Partition} (h : Dominates μ ν) : ν ≤ μ

decls.name: TauCeti.indiscrete_dominates
decls.doc: The one-part partition dominates every partition of the same natural number.
decls.statement:
theorem indiscrete_dominates {n : ℕ} (μ : n.Partition) :
    Dominates (Nat.Partition.indiscrete n) μ

decls.name: TauCeti.dominates_indiscrete_iff
decls.doc: A partition dominates the one-part partition only when it is that partition.
decls.statement:
theorem dominates_indiscrete_iff {n : ℕ} {μ : n.Partition} :
    Dominates μ (Nat.Partition.indiscrete n) ↔ μ = Nat.Partition.indiscrete n

decls.name: TauCeti.YoungDiagram.card_transpose
decls.doc: Transposing a Young diagram preserves its number of cells.
decls.statement: theorem card_transpose (μ : YoungDiagram) : μ.transpose.card = μ.card

decls.name: TauCeti.YoungDiagram.sum_rowLens
decls.doc: The sum of the row lengths of a Young diagram is its number of cells.
decls.statement: theorem sum_rowLens (μ : YoungDiagram) : μ.rowLens.sum = μ.card

decls.name: TauCeti.YoungDiagram.arm
decls.doc:
The arm of the cell `c` in the Young diagram `μ`: the cells of `μ` lying strictly to the right
of `c` in the same row.
decls.statement: def arm : Finset (ℕ × ℕ)

decls.name: TauCeti.YoungDiagram.leg
decls.doc:
The leg of the cell `c` in the Young diagram `μ`: the cells of `μ` lying strictly below `c` in
the same column.
decls.statement: def leg : Finset (ℕ × ℕ)

decls.name: TauCeti.YoungDiagram.hook
decls.doc:
The hook of the cell `c` in the Young diagram `μ`: the cell itself together with its arm and its
leg.
decls.statement: def hook : Finset (ℕ × ℕ)

decls.name: TauCeti.YoungDiagram.mem_arm
decls.statement: theorem mem_arm {d : ℕ × ℕ} : d ∈ arm μ c ↔ d ∈ μ ∧ d.1 = c.1 ∧ c.2 < d.2

decls.name: TauCeti.YoungDiagram.mem_leg
decls.statement: theorem mem_leg {d : ℕ × ℕ} : d ∈ leg μ c ↔ d ∈ μ ∧ d.2 = c.2 ∧ c.1 < d.1

decls.name: TauCeti.YoungDiagram.mem_hook
decls.statement:
theorem mem_hook {d : ℕ × ℕ} :
    d ∈ hook μ c ↔ d = c ∨ (d ∈ μ ∧ d.1 = c.1 ∧ c.2 < d.2) ∨ (d ∈ μ ∧ d.2 = c.2 ∧ c.1 < d.1)

decls.name: TauCeti.YoungDiagram.mem_hook_self
decls.statement: theorem mem_hook_self : c ∈ hook μ c

decls.name: TauCeti.YoungDiagram.arm_subset_cells
decls.statement: theorem arm_subset_cells : arm μ c ⊆ μ.cells

decls.name: TauCeti.YoungDiagram.leg_subset_cells
decls.statement: theorem leg_subset_cells : leg μ c ⊆ μ.cells

decls.name: TauCeti.YoungDiagram.hook_subset_cells
decls.statement: theorem hook_subset_cells (h : c ∈ μ) : hook μ c ⊆ μ.cells

decls.name: TauCeti.YoungDiagram.notMem_arm_self
decls.statement: theorem notMem_arm_self : c ∉ arm μ c

decls.name: TauCeti.YoungDiagram.notMem_leg_self
decls.statement: theorem notMem_leg_self : c ∉ leg μ c

decls.name: TauCeti.YoungDiagram.disjoint_arm_leg
decls.statement: theorem disjoint_arm_leg : Disjoint (arm μ c) (leg μ c)

decls.name: TauCeti.YoungDiagram.armLength
decls.doc:
The arm length of the cell `c` in the Young diagram `μ`: the number of cells of `μ` strictly to
the right of `c` in the same row.
decls.statement: def armLength : ℕ

decls.name: TauCeti.YoungDiagram.legLength
decls.doc:
The leg length of the cell `c` in the Young diagram `μ`: the number of cells of `μ` strictly
below `c` in the same column.
decls.statement: def legLength : ℕ

decls.name: TauCeti.YoungDiagram.hookLength
decls.doc: The hook length of the cell `c` in the Young diagram `μ`: the number of cells in its hook.
decls.statement: def hookLength : ℕ

decls.name: TauCeti.YoungDiagram.armLength_def
decls.doc: The arm length of a cell counts the columns of its row beyond it.
decls.statement: theorem armLength_def : armLength μ c = μ.rowLen c.1 - c.2 - 1

decls.name: TauCeti.YoungDiagram.legLength_def
decls.doc: The leg length of a cell counts the rows of its column beyond it.
decls.statement: theorem legLength_def : legLength μ c = μ.colLen c.2 - c.1 - 1

decls.name: TauCeti.YoungDiagram.hookLength_def
decls.doc: The hook length of a cell is its arm length plus its leg length plus one, the cell itself.
decls.statement: theorem hookLength_def : hookLength μ c = armLength μ c + legLength μ c + 1

decls.name: TauCeti.YoungDiagram.card_arm
decls.doc: The arm of a cell has `armLength` many elements.
decls.statement: theorem card_arm : (arm μ c).card = armLength μ c

decls.name: TauCeti.YoungDiagram.card_leg
decls.doc: The leg of a cell has `legLength` many elements.
decls.statement: theorem card_leg : (leg μ c).card = legLength μ c

decls.name: TauCeti.YoungDiagram.card_hook
decls.doc:
The hook of a cell has `hookLength` many elements: the numerical definition of `hookLength`
really does count the cells of the hook.
decls.statement: theorem card_hook : (hook μ c).card = hookLength μ c

decls.name: TauCeti.YoungDiagram.hookLength_pos
decls.statement: theorem hookLength_pos : 0 < hookLength μ c

decls.name: TauCeti.YoungDiagram.hookLength_le_card
decls.doc: A cell of the diagram has hook length at most the size of the diagram.
decls.statement: theorem hookLength_le_card (h : c ∈ μ) : hookLength μ c ≤ μ.card

decls.name: TauCeti.YoungDiagram.arm_transpose
decls.doc:
Transposition exchanges arms with legs: the arm of `c` in `μ.transpose` is the reflection of
the leg of `c.swap` in `μ`.
decls.statement:
theorem arm_transpose :
    arm μ.transpose c = (leg μ c.swap).map (Equiv.prodComm ℕ ℕ).toEmbedding

decls.name: TauCeti.YoungDiagram.leg_transpose
decls.doc:
Transposition exchanges legs with arms: the leg of `c` in `μ.transpose` is the reflection of
the arm of `c.swap` in `μ`.
decls.statement:
theorem leg_transpose :
    leg μ.transpose c = (arm μ c.swap).map (Equiv.prodComm ℕ ℕ).toEmbedding

decls.name: TauCeti.YoungDiagram.hook_transpose
decls.doc:
Transposition reflects hooks: the hook of `c` in `μ.transpose` is the reflection of the hook of
`c.swap` in `μ`.
decls.statement:
theorem hook_transpose :
    hook μ.transpose c = (hook μ c.swap).map (Equiv.prodComm ℕ ℕ).toEmbedding

decls.name: TauCeti.YoungDiagram.armLength_transpose
decls.doc: Transposition exchanges arm lengths with leg lengths.
decls.statement: theorem armLength_transpose : armLength μ.transpose c = legLength μ c.swap

decls.name: TauCeti.YoungDiagram.legLength_transpose
decls.doc: Transposition exchanges leg lengths with arm lengths.
decls.statement: theorem legLength_transpose : legLength μ.transpose c = armLength μ c.swap

decls.name: TauCeti.YoungDiagram.hookLength_transpose
decls.doc:
Transposition preserves hook lengths: the hook length of `c` in `μ.transpose` is that of
`c.swap` in `μ`.
decls.statement: theorem hookLength_transpose : hookLength μ.transpose c = hookLength μ c.swap

decls.name: TauCeti.YoungDiagram.prod_hookLength_transpose
decls.doc:
Transposing a Young diagram permutes its cells, and hence its hook lengths; in particular the
product of all hook lengths is a transposition invariant.
decls.statement:
theorem prod_hookLength_transpose :
    ∏ c ∈ μ.transpose.cells, hookLength μ.transpose c = ∏ c ∈ μ.cells, hookLength μ c

decls.name: TauCeti.YoungDiagram.armLength_eq_zero_iff
decls.statement: theorem armLength_eq_zero_iff : armLength μ c = 0 ↔ (c.1, c.2 + 1) ∉ μ

decls.name: TauCeti.YoungDiagram.legLength_eq_zero_iff
decls.statement: theorem legLength_eq_zero_iff : legLength μ c = 0 ↔ (c.1 + 1, c.2) ∉ μ

decls.name: TauCeti.YoungDiagram.hookLength_eq_one_iff
decls.doc:
A cell has hook length `1` exactly when the cell to its right and the cell below it are both
absent from the diagram; for a cell of `μ` this says that it is a corner.
decls.statement:
theorem hookLength_eq_one_iff :
    hookLength μ c = 1 ↔ (c.1, c.2 + 1) ∉ μ ∧ (c.1 + 1, c.2) ∉ μ

decls.name: TauCeti.YoungDiagram.hookLength_lt_hookLength_of_col_lt
decls.doc: Hook lengths strictly decrease from left to right along a row.

decls.name: TauCeti.YoungDiagram.hookLength_lt_hookLength_of_row_lt
decls.doc: Hook lengths strictly decrease from top to bottom down a column.

decls.name: TauCeti.YoungDiagram.cells_eq_of_colLen_le_one
decls.statement:
theorem cells_eq_of_colLen_le_one {μ : YoungDiagram} (h : μ.colLen 0 ≤ 1) :
    μ.cells = {0} ×ˢ Finset.range (μ.rowLen 0)

decls.name: TauCeti.YoungDiagram.card_eq_rowLen_of_colLen_le_one
decls.statement:
theorem card_eq_rowLen_of_colLen_le_one {μ : YoungDiagram} (h : μ.colLen 0 ≤ 1) :
    μ.card = μ.rowLen 0

decls.name: TauCeti.YoungDiagram.hookLength_eq_rowLen_sub_of_colLen_le_one
TauCeti.YoungDiagram.prod_hookLength_eq_factorial_of_colLen_le_one
decls.doc:
The hook-length formula for a Young diagram with at most one row: the hook lengths multiply to
`μ.card !`.
decls.statement:
theorem prod_hookLength_eq_factorial_of_colLen_le_one {μ : YoungDiagram} (h : μ.colLen 0 ≤ 1) :
    ∏ c ∈ μ.cells, hookLength μ c = Nat.factorial μ.card

decls.name: TauCeti.YoungDiagram.prod_hookLength_eq_factorial_of_rowLen_le_one
decls.doc:
The hook-length formula for a Young diagram with at most one column: the hook lengths multiply
to `μ.card !`.
decls.statement:
theorem prod_hookLength_eq_factorial_of_rowLen_le_one {μ : YoungDiagram} (h : μ.rowLen 0 ≤ 1) :
    ∏ c ∈ μ.cells, hookLength μ c = Nat.factorial μ.card

decls.name: TauCeti.partitionEquivYoungDiagram
decls.doc: Partitions of `n` are equivalent to Young diagrams with `n` cells.
decls.statement:
def partitionEquivYoungDiagram (n : ℕ) :
    n.Partition ≃ {μ : YoungDiagram // μ.card = n}

decls.name: TauCeti.partitionEquivYoungDiagram_apply_coe
decls.doc:
The Young diagram associated to a partition is the one built from its decreasing parts by
`YoungDiagram.ofRowLens`.
decls.statement:
theorem partitionEquivYoungDiagram_apply_coe (n : ℕ) (p : n.Partition) :
    (partitionEquivYoungDiagram n p).1 =
      _root_.YoungDiagram.ofRowLens (p.parts.sort (· ≥ ·))
        (Multiset.pairwise_sort p.parts (· ≥ ·)).sortedGE

decls.name: TauCeti.partitionEquivYoungDiagram_apply_rowLens
decls.doc: The Young diagram associated to a partition has its decreasing parts as row lengths.
decls.statement:
theorem partitionEquivYoungDiagram_apply_rowLens (n : ℕ) (p : n.Partition) :
    (partitionEquivYoungDiagram n p).1.rowLens = p.parts.sort (· ≥ ·)

decls.name: TauCeti.partitionEquivYoungDiagram_symm_apply_parts
decls.doc: Reading the row lengths of a sized Young diagram recovers the partition's parts.
decls.statement:
theorem partitionEquivYoungDiagram_symm_apply_parts (n : ℕ)
    (μ : {μ : YoungDiagram // μ.card = n}) :
    ((partitionEquivYoungDiagram n).symm μ).parts = μ.1.rowLens

decls.name: TauCeti.StandardYoungTableau
decls.doc:
A standard Young tableau of shape `μ` is a bijective labeling of its cells by
`Fin μ.card`, strictly increasing along rows and columns.
decls.statement: structure StandardYoungTableau (μ : YoungDiagram)

decls.name: TauCeti.StandardYoungTableau.instFunLike
decls.statement:
instance instFunLike {μ : YoungDiagram} :
    FunLike (StandardYoungTableau μ) ↥μ.cells (Fin μ.card)

decls.name: TauCeti.StandardYoungTableau.coe_toEquiv
decls.doc: The underlying function of a standard Young tableau is its labeling equivalence.
decls.statement:
theorem coe_toEquiv {μ : YoungDiagram} (T : StandardYoungTableau μ) :
    ⇑T.toEquiv = T

decls.name: TauCeti.StandardYoungTableau.toEquiv_apply
decls.doc: Evaluating the labeling equivalence agrees with evaluating the tableau.
decls.statement:
theorem toEquiv_apply {μ : YoungDiagram} (T : StandardYoungTableau μ) (c : ↥μ.cells) :
    T.toEquiv c = T c

decls.name: TauCeti.StandardYoungTableau.ext
decls.doc: Two standard Young tableaux are equal when all of their entries agree.
decls.statement:
theorem ext {μ : YoungDiagram} {T U : StandardYoungTableau μ}
    (h : ∀ c, T c = U c) : T = U

decls.name: TauCeti.StandardYoungTableau.bijective
decls.doc: The entries of a standard Young tableau form a bijection.
decls.statement:
theorem bijective {μ : YoungDiagram} (T : StandardYoungTableau μ) :
    Function.Bijective T

decls.name: TauCeti.StandardYoungTableau.injective
decls.doc: The entries of a standard Young tableau are injective.
decls.statement:
theorem injective {μ : YoungDiagram} (T : StandardYoungTableau μ) :
    Function.Injective T

decls.name: TauCeti.StandardYoungTableau.surjective
decls.doc: Every label occurs in a standard Young tableau.
decls.statement:
theorem surjective {μ : YoungDiagram} (T : StandardYoungTableau μ) :
    Function.Surjective T

decls.name: TauCeti.StandardYoungTableau.row_strict
decls.doc: Entries of a standard Young tableau increase strictly from left to right.
decls.statement:
theorem row_strict {μ : YoungDiagram} (T : StandardYoungTableau μ)
    {i j₁ j₂ : ℕ} (h : j₁ < j₂) (hcell : (i, j₂) ∈ μ) :
    T ⟨(i, j₁), μ.up_left_mem (by rfl) h.le hcell⟩ < T ⟨(i, j₂), hcell⟩

decls.name: TauCeti.StandardYoungTableau.col_strict
decls.doc: Entries of a standard Young tableau increase strictly from top to bottom.
decls.statement:
theorem col_strict {μ : YoungDiagram} (T : StandardYoungTableau μ)
    {i₁ i₂ j : ℕ} (h : i₁ < i₂) (hcell : (i₂, j) ∈ μ) :
    T ⟨(i₁, j), μ.up_left_mem h.le (by rfl) hcell⟩ < T ⟨(i₂, j), hcell⟩

decls.name: TauCeti.StandardYoungTableau.transposeCellEquiv
decls.statement: def transposeCellEquiv (μ : YoungDiagram) : ↥μ.transpose.cells ≃ ↥μ.cells

decls.name: TauCeti.StandardYoungTableau.transposeCellEquiv_apply
decls.statement:
theorem transposeCellEquiv_apply (μ : YoungDiagram) (c : ↥μ.transpose.cells) :
    transposeCellEquiv μ c = ⟨c.1.swap, YoungDiagram.mem_transpose.mp c.2⟩

decls.name: TauCeti.StandardYoungTableau.transposeCellEquiv_symm_apply
decls.statement:
theorem transposeCellEquiv_symm_apply (μ : YoungDiagram) (c : ↥μ.cells) :
    (transposeCellEquiv μ).symm c =
      ⟨c.1.swap, YoungDiagram.mem_transpose.mpr c.2⟩

decls.name: TauCeti.StandardYoungTableau.transpose
decls.doc:
Transpose a standard Young tableau by swapping its rows and columns while preserving its
labels.
decls.statement:
def transpose {μ : YoungDiagram} (T : StandardYoungTableau μ) :
    StandardYoungTableau μ.transpose

decls.name: TauCeti.StandardYoungTableau.transpose_apply_val
decls.doc: Transposition preserves the numeric label of each cell.
decls.statement:
theorem transpose_apply_val {μ : YoungDiagram} (T : StandardYoungTableau μ)
    (c : ↥μ.transpose.cells) :
    (T.transpose c).val =
      (T ⟨c.1.swap, YoungDiagram.mem_transpose.mp c.2⟩).val

decls.name: TauCeti.StandardYoungTableau.untranspose
decls.statement:
def untranspose {μ : YoungDiagram} (T : StandardYoungTableau μ.transpose) :
    StandardYoungTableau μ

decls.name: TauCeti.StandardYoungTableau.untranspose_apply_val
decls.statement:
theorem untranspose_apply_val {μ : YoungDiagram}
    (T : StandardYoungTableau μ.transpose) (c : ↥μ.cells) :
    (untranspose T c).val =
      (T ⟨c.1.swap, YoungDiagram.mem_transpose.mpr c.2⟩).val

decls.name: TauCeti.StandardYoungTableau.transposeEquiv
decls.doc: Transposition is an equivalence between standard Young tableaux of conjugate shapes.
decls.statement:
def transposeEquiv (μ : YoungDiagram) :
    StandardYoungTableau μ ≃ StandardYoungTableau μ.transpose

decls.name: TauCeti.StandardYoungTableau.transposeEquiv_apply
decls.doc: The forward map of `transposeEquiv` is tableau transposition.
decls.statement:
theorem transposeEquiv_apply {μ : YoungDiagram} (T : StandardYoungTableau μ) :
    transposeEquiv μ T = T.transpose

decls.name: TauCeti.StandardYoungTableau.transposeEquiv_symm_apply_val
decls.doc: The inverse transpose equivalence swaps cells while preserving their numeric labels.
decls.statement:
theorem transposeEquiv_symm_apply_val {μ : YoungDiagram}
    (T : StandardYoungTableau μ.transpose) (c : ↥μ.cells) :
    (((transposeEquiv μ).symm T) c).val =
      (T ⟨c.1.swap, YoungDiagram.mem_transpose.mpr c.2⟩).val

decls.name: TauCeti.StandardYoungTableau.instFintype
decls.doc: Standard Young tableaux of a fixed shape form a finite type.
decls.statement:
instance instFintype (μ : YoungDiagram) :
    Fintype (StandardYoungTableau μ)

decls.name: TauCeti.standardCount
decls.doc: The number of standard Young tableaux of shape `μ`.
decls.statement: def standardCount (μ : YoungDiagram) : ℕ

decls.name: TauCeti.standardCount_def
decls.doc: The number of standard Young tableaux is the cardinality of their finite type.
decls.statement:
theorem standardCount_def (μ : YoungDiagram) :
    standardCount μ = Fintype.card (StandardYoungTableau μ)

decls.name: TauCeti.standardCount_transpose
decls.doc: Transposing a Young diagram does not change its number of standard Young tableaux.
decls.statement:
theorem standardCount_transpose (μ : YoungDiagram) :
    standardCount μ.transpose = standardCount μ

decls.name: TauCeti.YoungTableau
decls.doc:
A `μ`-tableau: a bijective filling of the cells of the Young diagram `μ` by the labels
`Fin μ.card`.
decls.statement: abbrev YoungTableau (μ : YoungDiagram) : Type

decls.name: TauCeti.YoungTableau.rowIndex
decls.doc: The row of the cell of `μ` carrying the label `k` in the tableau `t`.
decls.statement: def rowIndex (t : YoungTableau μ) (k : Fin μ.card) : ℕ

decls.name: TauCeti.YoungTableau.colIndex
decls.doc: The column of the cell of `μ` carrying the label `k` in the tableau `t`.
decls.statement: def colIndex (t : YoungTableau μ) (k : Fin μ.card) : ℕ

decls.name: TauCeti.YoungTableau.rowIndex_def
decls.doc:
The row of a label is the first coordinate of the cell carrying it.  This is not a `simp`
lemma: `rowIndex` is the normal form, and `rowIndex_apply` computes it on a label presented as
the value of `t`.
decls.statement:
theorem rowIndex_def (t : YoungTableau μ) (k : Fin μ.card) :
    rowIndex t k = (t.symm k : ℕ × ℕ).1

decls.name: TauCeti.YoungTableau.colIndex_def
decls.doc:
The column of a label is the second coordinate of the cell carrying it.  As for
`rowIndex_def`, this is not a `simp` lemma.
decls.statement:
theorem colIndex_def (t : YoungTableau μ) (k : Fin μ.card) :
    colIndex t k = (t.symm k : ℕ × ℕ).2

decls.name: TauCeti.YoungTableau.rowIndex_apply
decls.statement:
theorem rowIndex_apply (t : YoungTableau μ) (c : ↥μ.cells) :
    rowIndex t (t c) = (c : ℕ × ℕ).1

decls.name: TauCeti.YoungTableau.colIndex_apply
decls.statement:
theorem colIndex_apply (t : YoungTableau μ) (c : ↥μ.cells) :
    colIndex t (t c) = (c : ℕ × ℕ).2

decls.name: TauCeti.YoungTableau.rowIndex_colIndex_injective
decls.doc:
A cell of a Young diagram is determined by its row together with its column, so a label of a
tableau is determined by its row and its column.
decls.statement:
theorem rowIndex_colIndex_injective (t : YoungTableau μ) :
    Function.Injective fun k => (rowIndex t k, colIndex t k)

decls.name: TauCeti.YoungTableau.rowFiberEquiv
decls.doc: The labels lying in row `i` of a `μ`-tableau are the cells of the `i`-th row of `μ`.
decls.statement:
def rowFiberEquiv (t : YoungTableau μ) (i : ℕ) :
    {k : Fin μ.card // rowIndex t k = i} ≃ ↥(μ.row i)

decls.name: TauCeti.YoungTableau.colFiberEquiv
decls.doc: The labels lying in column `j` of a `μ`-tableau are the cells of the `j`-th column of `μ`.
decls.statement:
def colFiberEquiv (t : YoungTableau μ) (j : ℕ) :
    {k : Fin μ.card // colIndex t k = j} ≃ ↥(μ.col j)

decls.name: TauCeti.YoungTableau.rowFiberEquiv_apply_coe
decls.statement:
theorem rowFiberEquiv_apply_coe (t : YoungTableau μ) (i : ℕ)
    (k : {k : Fin μ.card // rowIndex t k = i}) :
    (rowFiberEquiv t i k : ℕ × ℕ) = (t.symm k.1 : ℕ × ℕ)

decls.name: TauCeti.YoungTableau.colFiberEquiv_apply_coe
decls.statement:
theorem colFiberEquiv_apply_coe (t : YoungTableau μ) (j : ℕ)
    (k : {k : Fin μ.card // colIndex t k = j}) :
    (colFiberEquiv t j k : ℕ × ℕ) = (t.symm k.1 : ℕ × ℕ)

decls.name: TauCeti.YoungTableau.rowFiberEquiv_symm_apply_coe
decls.doc: The label attached to a cell of row `i` is the label of that cell in the tableau.
decls.statement:
theorem rowFiberEquiv_symm_apply_coe (t : YoungTableau μ) (i : ℕ) (c : ↥(μ.row i)) :
    ((rowFiberEquiv t i).symm c : Fin μ.card) =
      t ⟨(c : ℕ × ℕ), (YoungDiagram.mem_cells _).mpr (YoungDiagram.mem_row_iff.mp c.2).1⟩

decls.name: TauCeti.YoungTableau.colFiberEquiv_symm_apply_coe
decls.doc: The label attached to a cell of column `j` is the label of that cell in the tableau.
decls.statement:
theorem colFiberEquiv_symm_apply_coe (t : YoungTableau μ) (j : ℕ) (c : ↥(μ.col j)) :
    ((colFiberEquiv t j).symm c : Fin μ.card) =
      t ⟨(c : ℕ × ℕ), (YoungDiagram.mem_cells _).mpr (YoungDiagram.mem_col_iff.mp c.2).1⟩

decls.name: TauCeti.YoungTableau.relabel
decls.doc:
The tableau `t` with its labels permuted by `σ`: the cell that `t` labels `k` is labelled
`σ k` by `relabel σ t`.

Relabeling is the left action of `Equiv.Perm (Fin μ.card)` on `YoungTableau μ` recorded by
`relabel_one` and `relabel_relabel`, and it is transitive by `exists_relabel_eq`.  It is not
registered as a `MulAction` instance because `YoungTableau μ` is an abbreviation for a type of
equivalences, so such an instance would fire on equivalences at large, far outside the tableaux
it is meant for.
decls.statement: def relabel (σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin μ.card)) (t : YoungTableau μ) : YoungTableau μ

decls.name: TauCeti.YoungTableau.relabel_apply
decls.statement:
theorem relabel_apply (σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin μ.card)) (t : YoungTableau μ) (c : ↥μ.cells) :
    relabel σ t c = σ (t c)

decls.name: TauCeti.YoungTableau.relabel_symm_apply
decls.statement:
theorem relabel_symm_apply (σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin μ.card)) (t : YoungTableau μ)
    (k : Fin μ.card) :
    (relabel σ t).symm k = t.symm (σ⁻¹ k)

decls.name: TauCeti.YoungTableau.rowIndex_relabel
decls.doc: Relabeling by `σ` moves the label `k` to the row that `t` gives to `σ⁻¹ k`.
decls.statement:
theorem rowIndex_relabel (σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin μ.card)) (t : YoungTableau μ) (k : Fin μ.card) :
    rowIndex (relabel σ t) k = rowIndex t (σ⁻¹ k)

decls.name: TauCeti.YoungTableau.colIndex_relabel
decls.doc: Relabeling by `σ` moves the label `k` to the column that `t` gives to `σ⁻¹ k`.
decls.statement:
theorem colIndex_relabel (σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin μ.card)) (t : YoungTableau μ) (k : Fin μ.card) :
    colIndex (relabel σ t) k = colIndex t (σ⁻¹ k)

decls.name: TauCeti.YoungTableau.relabel_one
decls.statement: theorem relabel_one (t : YoungTableau μ) : relabel 1 t = t

decls.name: TauCeti.YoungTableau.relabel_relabel
decls.statement:
theorem relabel_relabel (σ τ : Equiv.Perm (Fin μ.card)) (t : YoungTableau μ) :
    relabel σ (relabel τ t) = relabel (σ * τ) t

decls.name: TauCeti.YoungTableau.relabelPerm
decls.doc:
The permutation of the labels carrying the tableau `t` to the tableau `t'` of the same
shape.
decls.statement: def relabelPerm (t t' : YoungTableau μ) : Equiv.Perm (Fin μ.card)

decls.name: TauCeti.YoungTableau.relabelPerm_apply
decls.doc:
The permutation carrying `t` to `t'` sends the label `k` to the label that `t'` gives to the
cell that `t` labels `k`.
decls.statement:
theorem relabelPerm_apply (t t' : YoungTableau μ) (k : Fin μ.card) :
    relabelPerm t t' k = t' (t.symm k)

decls.name: TauCeti.YoungTableau.relabel_relabelPerm
decls.statement: theorem relabel_relabelPerm (t t' : YoungTableau μ) : relabel (relabelPerm t t') t = t'

decls.name: TauCeti.YoungTableau.exists_relabel_eq
decls.doc: Any two tableaux of the same shape differ by a relabeling.
decls.statement: theorem exists_relabel_eq (t t' : YoungTableau μ) : ∃ σ, relabel σ t = t'
